findings.current: It was questionable whether it could even be moved in one piece.
findings.defect: The assembled copy omits the creature’s stated size: from head to tail, it was over a hundred zhang long. The baseline preserves this measurement, and the translation even retains a footnote defining zhang despite omitting the measurement.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly gives the corpse’s length and uses that scale to support the difficulty of moving it whole and keeping the matter secret.
findings.replacement: From head to tail, the giant creature stretched for more than a hundred zhang.[^1] It was questionable whether it could even be moved in one piece.

findings.current: Perhaps because they had belonged to a five-hundred-year-old imugi, the bones had a luster unlike anything else.
findings.defect: The translation drops the image of the enormous bones visible between the split scales and gaping wounds, radiating a faint glow.
findings.rationale: The source establishes both the bones’ visible placement in the corpse and their faint glow; the accepted baseline preserves that image.
findings.replacement: Between the split scales and gaping wounds, enormous bones radiated a faint glow. Perhaps because they had belonged to a five-hundred-year-old imugi, the bones had a luster unlike anything else.

summary: The translation is largely faithful, but it omits two concrete physical details preserved in the accepted baseline.
